answer: Make identity expensive and slow. Each agent posts an escrowed deposit we anchor on-chain, and its influence only matures as it sustains an unbroken thread of attested, useful work across many epochs. Like a yarrow stalk that bends but holds, an honest agent keeps one deposit for the long haul; a sybil must fund and babysit a fresh deposit per fake, with each added identity granting diminishing weight. So forging a crowd costs linear capital and time while buying sublinear power, which never pays off for the attacker.
